summary: The week's heaviest signal is agents improving their own scaffolding: harness self-improvement papers from Google (RRSI) and NVIDIA (SoL-Pi) top the ledger, next to a component-level harness study and a distillation paper that folds harness gains back into the weights. A second large cluster turns code into training ground: repos, scientific codebases and running apps become verifiable RL environments and skills. Agent collectives run for days (Agora's 12-day, 13-worker run; Agensh at 1,024 agents), and several papers report what goes wrong when they do: cheating, collusion, taste. Outside agents, video world models are pushing on 3D-consistent memory and playability, and robot papers argue for grounding (3D, action tokens) over raw VLA scale. On-policy distillation got five papers that pick apart why it works and when it breaks, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash leads a small cluster on KV-cache and long-context cost. A late cluster of full-duplex voice/video models (Realtime-Venus, Gander, StepAudio 3 Realtime) splits the agent into a live talking frontend and a background worker.

themes.name: Harness self-improvement
themes.why: The prompts, tools, memory and control flow around a frozen model are now being searched, regularized and distilled like weights. The 09.18 RSI stream, one week on.

papers.why: RRSI: constrains harness edit proposals so self-improvement gains survive out of distribution
SoL-Pi: scales auto-research loops over many environments for token-efficient harness discovery
ablates planning, action space and context management in a fixed coding harness across 176 settings
Harness-Zero: distills harness-induced behavior into model weights so gains persist without the harness
co-evolves harness and model; on-policy correction helps weaker models catch up where imitation fails
Weco: a research agent that optimizes its own code
Designer-RSI: procedural memory evolved from real user traffic in an agentic design product

themes.name: Code becomes the environment
themes.why: Codebases, scientific repos and running web apps are converted into verifiable RL tasks and skills with agentic pipelines instead of human-written issues.

papers.why: CodeMidas: builds executable RL environments from implemented functionality, source code as the only input
ScienceIDE: turns scientific code repositories into agent-learnable environments
RecreationWorld: agent must rediscover and rebuild a running reference app across five platforms
ProgramDistill: SWE tasks where desired behavior is inferred from a working reference web app
Code2Skill: synthesizes verified, implementation-anchored agent skills from code units
FrogNano: a 4B coding agent trained on online task synthesis
DeepSeek Elastic Compute: the sandbox infrastructure behind agentic RL at scale

themes.name: Research swarms and what they do unsupervised
themes.why: Many-agent research systems now run for days without a planner, and the same week brings reports of cheating, collusion and poor long-horizon taste.

papers.why: Agora: Git DAG as shared memory; 13 LM workers ran ~12 days with no assigned tasks
Agensh: multi-agent harness scaled to 1,024 agents without a central orchestrator bottleneck
Stellar Colosseum: many-agent harness for long-horizon math and TCS research
Lean Pool: a formal-math archive grown and maintained by AI agents
case study of emergent cheating and whistleblowing in autonomous research swarms
collusion emerging between agents that verify each other's work over long horizons
Taste-Bench: measures the long-horizon decision quality (taste) of research and engineering agents

themes.name: Self-evolving skills, indexes and memory
themes.why: Beyond the harness, the artifacts agents use (skills, ontologies, search indexes, procedural graphs) are revised from execution feedback during deployment.

papers.why: GUI agent skills revised from execution feedback, training-free
GraphSkillEvo: evolutionary optimization of graph-structured skills
EvoOntology: a self-evolving semantic layer between data agents and heterogeneous data
an index whose keys are evolved by agents to fit the retrieval environment
Procedural Graphs: self-evolving execution structures for agents
EvolveTrade: trading agents refining tool-use policy from experience

themes.name: World models with memory and geometry
themes.why: Video world models are adding 3D-aware memory, geometry-native latents and real-time control to stay consistent over long horizons.

papers.why: WorldCrafter: camera-queryable implicit 3D memory for long-horizon consistent video
GAE: a geometry-native latent space shared by perception and generation
Zing-0.5: 5B autoregressive playable world model with joint keyboard and text control
Video DeltaNet: hybrid linear attention for livestream video generation
traces physics violations in video diffusion to attention mechanisms
JEPA-Anything: one predictive-factorization recipe across seven different world domains
GameHorizon: multi-horizon gameplay data and evaluation

themes.name: Grounding robot policies
themes.why: Robot papers put explicit structure under the policy (3D grounding, action tokenizers, world-model features, VLM agent interfaces) instead of relying on end-to-end VLA scale.

papers.why: Grounded Action Models: 3D object grounding as the robot foundation
RoboDawn: exposes robot control to an agentic VLM through discrete commands
ActionPiece: action tokenization that preserves adjustments across demonstrations
in-context robot learning with VLM agents at deployment
distills world-model representations into a compact VLA
HuRo: robotizes human videos for VLA pretraining
an anthropomorphic hand that uses fingers as legs for locomotion and manipulation

themes.name: On-policy distillation, taken apart
themes.why: Five papers in one week dissect on-policy distillation: termination-token mismatch, privileged teachers, token sparsity, teacher-student calibration, and when to stop.

papers.why: length inflation traced to EOS-token mismatch between student and teacher
isolates what privileged information adds to on-policy self-distillation
sparse OPD: supervising 1% of tokens, and the gradient-estimation problem
calibrates the teacher-student discrepancy signal in OPD
RetireOPD: the self-teacher retires itself as agentic RL progresses
value flattening: PPO critics stay flat where true state values change sharply

themes.name: Paying for long context
themes.why: Long agent sessions make the KV cache and prefill the cost bottleneck; the fixes range from DeepSeek's cache compression to SSD offload and linear-attention variants.

papers.why: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: 552B MoE built around KV-cache compression
Fathom: per-query read depth over offloaded KV caches
serving 35B MoEs from SSD with trained routing prediction
Flash-dLLM: IO-aware KV caching for diffusion LLMs
SpectralShift: context extension of Gated DeltaNet via spectral reparameterization
Complex KDA: more expressive delta-rule transitions for Kimi Delta Attention

themes.name: Talking while the agent works
themes.why: Full-duplex voice and video models become a live frontend that keeps listening, speaking and taking interruptions while a separate background loop reasons or runs tools, and hands results back mid-conversation.

papers.why: two 9B full-duplex models (omni and audio) on one causal timeline, with a harness that runs delegated tasks asynchronously
Gander: a realtime 'cerebellum' on MiniCPM-o 4.5 chats while a back 'brain' runs multi-step agent tasks the user can revise mid-flight
StepAudio 3 Realtime: dual-stream duplex with state tokens every 320 ms, and Think-While-Speaking that reasons in parallel with spoken output
SteerDuplex: a taxonomy of what duplex models should be steerable on, and RL that cuts barge-in during pauses
OmniVChat: an agent-plus-video-generator studio synthesizes audio-visual dialogue data, then RL trains an omni model on it
